subject: Throughput/latency flare — rapid response plan & customer comms
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.example.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.example.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com>, ops@fastcart.com
Cc:
Date: Fri, 05 Oct 2028 07:12:00 -0700
Subject: [INCIDENT] sudden p95/p99 lift for gen-api serving FastCart — first alert

Monitoring observed an abrupt p95/p99 latency lift and throughput drop on the gen-api pool serving FastCart starting 07:06 PDT. Key symptoms:
- Inbound request rate steady, but per-token generation latency jumped ~3x for a subset of routes (checkout/confirm, pricing/recalculate).
- Autoscale did not add additional workers due to constant slot counts hitting per-model constraint.
- Prefix cache eviction spikes for 2 worker hosts.

Initial impact: 10-15% of customer traffic saw >2s extra tail latency; overall throughput for FastCart down ~18% for 07:06-07:10 window.

Immediate asks:
1) Engineering (Karthik/Ben): collect traces + KV cache metrics, check kernel scheduling changes from last deploy. I attached initial traces.
2) Product/CS (Vivek/Marissa): I recommend we open a short incident channel and prepare a one-paragraph customer note we can send in 20–30 mins.

I'll keep collecting traces and will update in 15 mins.

--
Ben Carter
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
Attachment: diagnostic-trace-20281005.tar.gz (10MB, tar.gz of worker traces)
From: Sam Patel <sam@fastcart.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.example.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.example.com>
Date: Fri, 05 Oct 2028 07:18:42 -0700
Subject: Re: [INCIDENT] sudden p95/p99 lift for gen-api serving FastCart — first alert

Thanks for the heads up. We're seeing checkout timeouts in our logs starting 07:08 — this is impacting checkout completion. Can you confirm whether this is limited to our tenant or broader? Need ETA on mitigation.

Sam
Ops Lead, FastCart

On Fri, Oct 5, 2028 at 07:12 Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.example.com> wrote:
> Monitoring observed an abrupt p95/p99 latency lift and throughput drop on the gen-api pool serving FastCart starting 07:06 PDT.
>
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.example.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.example.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example.com>
Cc: ops@fastcart.com
Date: Fri, 05 Oct 2028 07:24:10 -07:00
Subject: Re: [INCIDENT] sudden p95/p99 lift for gen-api serving FastCart — rapid plan + customer note (draft)

Quick plan and product asks below — please confirm feasibility ASAP. I pasted a draft customer note at the bottom; Marissa, can you trigger that once we have a confirmed mitigation ETA?

Tech plan (Ben/Karthik):
- Short-term (5–20 mins): isolate affected worker hosts and force prefix cache warming on cold hosts. If we can safely evict a single worker and restart it to clear kernel scheduling pressure, do that.
- Medium-term (30–90 mins): open temporary routing to the replicated gen-api pool in us-west-2 to restore throughput for FastCart while we investigate root cause. This requires a routing policy exception (prod override) from product.
- Longer-term: add a per-tenant fallback to a lower-latency model variant when tail exceeds SLA; product to scope cadence.

Product asks (for roadmap/ops):
1) Approve temporary routing override for FastCart to us-west-2 replicated pool. This is emergency-only and will be revoked once we confirm stability.
2) Prioritize a small work item to add tenant-scoped soft-fallback for next sprint (planning).
3) Approve a one-time credit if we need to route significant traffic off primary pool (finance sign-off later).

Draft customer note (suggested):
"FastCart — we're investigating a transient increase in model latency that is impacting a portion of your requests. Our team is executing mitigation now to restore throughput; we expect a measurable improvement within 30 minutes and will follow up with a status update in 60 minutes. Apologies for the disruption — we'll share root-cause details and any compensating credits if applicable."

Ben/Karthik: can you reply with ETA for the short-term mitigation and whether the routing override is safe to apply? Marissa: stand by to send the customer note with the ETA.

--
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.example.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.example.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example.com>, ops@fastcart.com
Date: Fri, 05 Oct 2028 07:31:55 -07:00
Subject: Re: [INCIDENT] sudden p95/p99 lift for gen-api serving FastCart — rapid plan + customer note (draft)

Status update: we've identified localized kernel preemption pressure on hosts gw-17/18 causing KV store I/O stalls and prefix cache misses. Short term actions taken (07:28–07:31):
- Recycled gw-18 (restart) — prefix cache warmed on restart, partial recovery seen.
- Forced sticky routing of 30% of FastCart traffic to secondary workers in same AZ to reduce contention.

Observed effect: p95 for affected routes reduced ~45% after restart and sticky routing; throughput recovering but still ~5–8% below baseline.

Routing override: we can route remaining traffic to the replicated pool in us-west-2 as a next step, but we need product sign-off to change routing policy for this tenant (temporary exception). Expected customer-visible improvement: full throughput recovery within 20–30 mins after cutover.

I'll prepare a concise checklist for the operation channel. Ben: please attach post-ops metrics and trace subset once available.

Karthik
Staff SW Eng, Inference Serving
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example.com>
To: Sam Patel <sam@fastcart.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.example.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.example.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com>
Date: Fri, 05 Oct 2028 07:43:05 -07:00
Subject: Re: [INCIDENT] sudden p95/p99 lift for gen-api serving FastCart — customer update

Sam — quick update from the team: we observed an increase in tail latency starting ~07:06. Engineering performed an isolated restart of an affected worker and implemented a sticky routing change; those steps reduced p95 by ~45% and throughput is recovering.

Next step: with your go-ahead we'll fail over remaining FastCart traffic to our replicated pool in us-west-2 as a temporary measure — we expect that action to restore normal throughput within ~20–30 minutes. We'll confirm once the failover completes and follow up with a timeline for RCA and any credit adjustments if applicable.

Do you want us to proceed with the temporary failover?

Thanks,
Marissa
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
Attachment: draft-customer-note-1015.txt
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.example.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.example.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example.com>
Cc: ops@fastcart.com
Date: Fri, 05 Oct 2028 13:45:00 -07:00
Subject: [INCIDENT] post-mitigation summary — FastCart latency/throughput flare (summary)

Final summary and next steps:
- Timeline: 07:06 incident start; 07:28 worker recycle + sticky routing; 07:40 routing override to us-west-2 completed; customer throughput returned to baseline by ~08:05.
- Root cause (preliminary): kernel preemption and I/O contention on two gateway workers triggering cascading prefix cache misses. No code regression identified; likely scheduling interaction with recent kernel and driver updates on those hosts.
- Impact: transient ~18% throughput reduction and p99 increase for ~60 minutes for FastCart only. Broader fleet unaffected.
- Actions taken: worker restarts, sticky routing, temporary cross-AZ failover to replicated pool.
- Follow-up items (owners):
  * Ben: collect full trace set and correlate with device driver updates (INF-9832).
  * Karthik: harden eviction/warming heuristics and add safeguard to prevent autoscaler from being blocked by slot constraints (next sprint).
  * Product (Vivek): scope tenant fallback work and approve any customer credits with finance.
  * CS (Marissa): coordinate customer RCA + credit comms; send postmortem within 3 business days.

Attachments: diagnostic-trace-20281005.tar.gz (full), perf-deltas.csv (summary).

Closing note: no further action required for customer-facing routing; we recommend scheduling a small controlled rollout of the new kernel/driver combo with extra telemetry.

--
Ben Carter
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
